reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 in the series. Game 2 was decided by the opponent's Altaria (Focus Sash / Cloud Nine / Tailwind / Helping Hand) enabling Mamoswine as a devastating breaker. Both Mega Charizard Y and Skarmory fainted on Turn 2 to simultaneous super-effective hits (Mamoswine Rock Slide OHKO'd Charizard Y; Armarouge Armor Cannon OHKO'd Skarmory), leaving only Meowscarada and Venusaur to clean up. Cloud Nine shut down sun, negating Venusaur's Chlorophyll and Charizard Y's value. Altaria's Helping Hand boosted Mamoswine's Icicle Crash past our remaining Pokémon, and Altaria's Moonblast finished Meowscarada on Turn 4. No hazards were ever set because Skarmory died before acting offensively. The opponent's speed control (Tailwind + natural speed) meant our revenge kills were unreliable.
reflections.adjustment: 1) Replace Skarmory with Toxapex or Swampert: Skarmory never set hazards and died uselessly on Turn 2. Toxapex offers Scald burns and bulk against Mamoswine; Swampert's Water/Ground typing walls Mamoswine and Ice coverage. 2) Consider leading with Venusaur or Torkoal instead of Charizard Y + Skarmory to guarantee hazard setup before committing the Mega slot. 3) Bring Aegislash over one of the weaker links — King's Shield baits Mamoswine's Rock Slide and threatens Swords Dance sweeps. 4) Against Altaria specifically: carry a faster Taunt user or a Pokémon that can 2HKO Altaria before Focus Sash activates (Meowscarada's Leaf Storm would OHKO but risks accuracy; a neutral Earth Power from Venusaur does not). 5) Sun team viability is questionable against this opponent — Cloud Nine hard-counters the entire sun strategy. Consider a balanced or rain pivot instead for a rematch.
reflections.notebook: OPPONENT TENDENCIES (durable): Altaria is their linchpin support — Focus Sash guarantees setup; Cloud Nine neutralizes sun; Tailwind + Helping Hand boost Mamoswine's speed and damage. Mamoswine is the primary win condition — Expert Belt, Thick Fat, Icicle Crash / Rock Slide coverage, Adamant nature. Expect it to clean up after Altaria softens. Armarouge is a glass cannon wallbreaker (Armor Cannon) but fell to priority; likely a one-game pick. Sneasler is probable 4th slot (unrevealed) — FakeOut + Jolly/Unburden makes it a fast revenge killer and lead threat. Opponent pivots heavily (Whirlwind, Helping Hand, U-turn implied). STRATEGIC FACTS: Sun is shut down by Cloud Nine — Venusaur and Charizard Y lose ~50% of their value. No hazards were set in either game — opponent kept a clean field. Meowscarada's Protean + Sucker Punch was the best performer but cannot be relied on to break Altaria + Mamoswine without chip damage. PREP CONCLUSIONS: Need a Cloud Nine answer (Taunt, faster Moonblast revenge, or remove sun dependency entirely). Bring bulkier pivots that survive +2 Expert Belt Mamoswine Ice coverage. Hazard stacking is mandatory — opponent's team lacks Defog, so even one layer of Rocks/Spikes swings late-game. Consider dropping sun outright for a more neutral offensive balance in a rematch.

reflections.summary: You won Game 2 and the series 2-0 by executing a strong anti-sun plan: Altaria established Tailwind and revealed Cloud Nine, while Mamoswine applied immediate Rock Slide and Icicle Crash pressure to Charizard, Skarmory, Meowscarada, and Venusaur. The four brought were well suited: Altaria and Mamoswine were the key pieces, and Armarouge traded itself for Skarmory after removing it with Armor Cannon; Dedenne was not needed. No friendly Mega Stone holder was registered or evolved. There were no decision errors or substitutions. The supplied evidence does not identify a specific between-game adjustment from Game 1, so its effect cannot be proven; the observable Game 2 plan clearly helped rather than backfired. The six registered were broadly appropriate, but no evidence shows that Farigiraf, Sinistcha, Meowstic-F, or Qwilfish offered a materially better four or set into this opponent.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a future series, preserve the Altaria-plus-Mamoswine core and prioritize early weather control, speed control, and spread or super-effective pressure on Charizard and Venusaur. Keep Armarouge available to punish Skarmory, but avoid exposing it unnecessarily to Meowscarada's Sucker Punch and Venusaur's Ground coverage. Consider bringing Dedenne only when its paralysis or support is specifically needed; the unused alternatives have no demonstrated advantage from this series. Since no Game 1 details were supplied, make future adjustments from confirmed scouting rather than assuming a particular between-game change worked.
reflections.notebook: Altaria's Cloud Nine and Tailwind are strong tools against the opponent's sun mode and should remain central. Charizard is Mega Charizard Y with Protect, Fire Blast, Solar Beam, and Focus Blast; expect sun pressure and possible Protect scouting. Venusaur has Chlorophyll, Growth, Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, and Earth Power, so it can exploit sun while also threatening Fire-types and Armarouge with Ground coverage. Meowscarada is Life Orb Protean with Leaf Storm, Play Rough, Brick Break, and Sucker Punch; respect priority and avoid relying on weakened Armarouge to move safely. Skarmory carries hazards, Whirlwind, and Roost and can disrupt setup or positioning, but it is vulnerable to strong Fire attacks. Torkoal and Aegislash were available but not brought in this game; do not assume they will be absent in a rematch. Mamoswine's Rock Slide and Icicle Crash gave immediate, valuable pressure into the sun roster, while Armarouge's Armor Cannon was effective into Skarmory. Future preparation should retain weather control, fast pressure, and protection against Sucker Punch and Earth Power.
